page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system delivers 128 GB of total system RAM, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core, characteristic of memory-heavy cloud tiers.

Hardware provisioning does not include integrated local disk storage, which necessitates network-attached cloud storage volumes for all OS installations and transactional data storage. Graphical acceleration is absent, with zero hardware GPUs attached. Networking features a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance by default.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory profile makes the server efficient for memory-saturated applications that do not require high vCPU counts. Because there is no bundled local NVMe capacity, workloads rely entirely on external block storage, representing an I/O tradeoff. The instance is suited for in-memory key-value databases, distributed cache systems such as Redis, relational databases with moderate query concurrency, and large-scale ETL data processing pipelines.

Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128 GB of RAM. This provides an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, catering to environments that require substantial random-access memory relative to processing cores. The instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data, and operates without discrete GPU hardware. Baseline network performance is configured at 5 Gbps. This resource balance makes the instance appropriate for memory-bound services, including in-memory caches, distributed memory grids, relational databases with extensive buffer pools, and big data preprocessing pipelines.
